correctness.rationale: For n>=2 let b count adjacent unequal pairs. The b incidences on zeros cover b−t distinct zeros, since exactly the centers of 101 are counted twice. Thus n−(b−t) replacements are allowed. Among the b potential swaps precisely two per such center are forbidden, without repeat swap positions even for overlapping occurrences. All allowed operations give distinct outputs by their changed-position sets. This gives degree n−t (also directly for n=1) and ball size one more. With k ones, choose c of the k−1 interior zero gaps to have length one, give all others two zeros, and allocate the residual n−3k+2+c across k+1−c variable gaps. Stars and bars yields the stated multiplicities and a geometric series in the number of gaps gives H(z,u). Spacing of starts and the words (10)^c followed by 1 and trailing zeros give exact support; at maximum c one must have k=c+1 for n>=3, with at most one extra zero in an exterior gap, giving the stated extremizers. Setting u=0 counts maximum-degree words. The small Fibonacci root stays simple and separated from other poles near u=1 for complex u; the nonzero amplitude and strict radius gap permit differentiating the simple-pole coefficient asymptotic via analyticity. Differentiating D(r(t),exp(t))=0 twice gives the two displayed cumulant slopes for d=n−t.
residual_risks: The complex-root argument, not finite numerical fits, proves the asymptotics. These are constrained linear one-edit neighborhoods (sphere excludes the center), with no wraparound or unrestricted outputs.

value.rationale: For a standard constrained edit graph, the histogram measures how one-error exposure varies by source and weight. The local characterization gives extremal neighborhoods and the variance gives a fluctuation scale neither determined by the prior mean nor by graph diameter. The distribution is for all lengths and usable for constrained-channel analysis without claiming a new packing bound.
residual_risks: No coding performance, construction or optimum is proved. The already-known mean is not the mathematical value added.
